decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent with one official dissenting in favor of a rate hike.

changes.quote: Household spending and business fixed investment have been increasing at solid rates in recent months, and the housing sector has improved further; however, net exports have been soft.
changes.explanation: The Committee updated its language to note that household spending and business investment are growing at solid rates.

changes.quote: The pace of job gains slowed and the unemployment rate held steady.
changes.explanation: This new sentence highlights a temporary slowdown in the pace of job gains while the unemployment rate remained unchanged.

changes.quote: The Committee continues to see the risks to the outlook for economic activity and the labor market as nearly balanced but is monitoring global economic and financial developments.
changes.explanation: The Fed added a specific reference to monitoring global economic and financial developments.

changes.quote: In determining whether it will be appropriate to raise the target range at its next meeting, the Committee will assess progress--both realized and expected--toward its objectives of maximum employment and 2 percent inflation.
changes.explanation: The Fed shifted its language to focus specifically on whether it will be appropriate to raise the target range at its next meeting.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee continues to see the risks to the outlook for economic activity and the labor market as nearly balanced but is monitoring global economic and financial developments.

The Committee anticipates that it will be appropriate to raise the target range for the federal funds rate when it has seen some further improvement in the labor market and is reasonably confident that inflation will move back to its 2 percent objective over the medium term.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.04% APR costs about $50.17 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.1% and moved +5 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.82% would rise by about $8.56 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 5%, and employers added an average of 189k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 0% over the past year (September 2015); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.2%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 1.6% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +8 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.23% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that future rate adjustments depend on continued improvement in the labor market and confidence that inflation will return to the 2 percent target. As an educational note, the forecast model indicates a 93 percent probability of a hold at the next meeting.

citations.detail: To support continued progress toward maximum employment and price stability, the Committee today reaffirmed its view that the current 0 to 1/4 percent target range for the federal funds rate remains appropriate.
